comments.note: CategoryEditorViewModel has no dedicated unit tests. All 5 AC were verified through code review only. The AC are logic-heavy (IsReadOnly guard, CanSave, CanDelete, CloseRequested event semantics) and should be covered by unit tests. Recommend adding CategoryEditorViewModelTests.cs covering at minimum: (1) IsDefault category — SaveCommand disabled; (2) IsMostUsed category — SaveCommand disabled; (3) empty name — SaveCommand disabled; (4) tagCount > 0 — DeleteCommand disabled; (5) create mode — DeleteCommand disabled.

CanSave guard is a defensive check inside Save() in addition to the RelayCommand CanExecute. This is correct and guards against direct Execute() calls. However, the existing-names list (_existingNames) is accepted in the constructor but never used in CanSave. The duplicate-name check is deferred debt — the list sits unused until the follow-up WP.

Save() uses Name.Trim() but CanSave() uses !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Name) without trimming. A name of '   ' (all spaces) would pass IsNullOrWhiteSpace check as false, so CanSave returns false. This is correct behavior but slightly implicit; a name of '  valid  ' would save as 'valid' (trimmed), which is desirable.
